correctness.rationale: For cubic H, a perfect external-edge-dominating set F has vertex selected degree 0,1,3, with L={degree0} independent and A_H 1_L=0 over F2; conversely the independent parity kernel constructs F uniquely. For GP(n,3), a_i=1_L(u_i), b_i=1_L(v_i)=a_{i-1}+a_{i+1} and the inner equations yield (1+T²+T⁴+T⁶+T⁸)a=0, hence (1+T^10)a=0. Thus sequences have period gcd(n,10) and reduction to at most 2^10 binary outer words is exhaustive. I independently enumerated every word of periods 1,2,5,10 and recovered counts {0:1},{0:1},{0:1,4:5},{0:1,4:10,6:20,8:5} by L size. Since |F|=3n-3|L|, this proves the complete stated polynomial for all n>=7 and clarifies the d=10 coefficients and minimum 5 matching sets. A finite direct edge-definition checker is part of the package; the all-n argument is the period reduction plus exhaustive finite table, not extrapolation.
residual_risks: Uses external-edge definition, labelled graph n>=7; not efficient domination of every selected edge.
